column1: f2d3cf|Which part does the robot need to "know whether there is a wall ahead"?
a3ba31|A motor makes the robot move; a sensor is what lets it "sense" its surroundings.

a531d1|

The Brain is like the robot's brain. The program you write is downloaded here, and the Brain runs it line by line, then commands the motors and sensors.

The Brain has a screen, buttons, and 12 ports (Smart Ports) for plugging in motors and sensors.
90cde2|Picture it: Brain = brain, Smart Cable = nerves, motors = muscles, sensors = eyes and ears.

4f8432|

A Smart Motor makes wheels turn, arms lift and claws open. What makes it "smart" is its built-in rotation measurement, so a program can tell it to "turn 2 rotations" or "turn to a certain angle".
2245e0|Faster isn't always better for a motor. Spinning too fast can make the robot slip and be inaccurate.

2712ab|

Sensors let the robot "know" what's going on:

  • Distance: how far away is something ahead?
  • Color: what color does it see?
  • Gyro: which way is the robot facing, and how many degrees has it turned?
  • Bumper: did it bump into something?
  • Touch LED: responds when touched, and can also show colors.

d7fb7b|

The Controller lets you drive the robot by hand with joysticks and buttons. Structural parts include beams, pins, connectors and more, used to build the body. Competition rules allow only official VEX IQ parts.

0eae94|To make the robot "stop when it hits a wall", which sensor is the most direct?
668791|The Bumper is built to detect whether it hit something. A Distance sensor could work too, but it measures "how much farther to go".
2180c1|What's the biggest difference between a Smart Motor and an ordinary toy motor?
e4d3a4|It has built-in rotation measurement, so a program can tell it to turn a set number of rotations or angle
996f3b|Built-in rotation measurement is what makes "turn 2 rotations" or "turn 90 degrees" so accurate.
877f64|Take out your real kit and get to know the parts you'll use.
3b2f10|Take out the Brain, a motor, a sensor and a Smart Cable.
0a240a|Take a photo with your phone and write each part's name and job next to it.

dd729b|Paste the photo and write down each part's name and job.
6c2e83|The motor is plugged into Port 3 on the Brain, but the program sets the device to Port 1. What happens?
21aa15|The motor doesn't move (or a different device acts up)
c419aa|The port number in the program must exactly match the port you actually plugged into.

d91f94|

The Brain has 12 Smart Ports, numbered 1–12. Every motor and every sensor plugs into one of them.

After plugging in, the program has to know "which device is on which port" — this is called configuring devices.

ae9167|

In VEXcode open Devices, add the motor or sensor you plugged in, pick the same port number, and give it an easy name (like leftMotor).

Once set up, the matching block category appears — for example, only after you add a distance sensor do you see the distance blocks.
742e82|Plugged into Port 3 but Devices says Port 1 — the most common reason for "why won't the motor move?"

3c3e62|

When two motors are mounted on the left and right of the robot, they are usually mounted facing opposite directions. If the program tells both to go "forward", one side's wheel actually turns backward and the robot just spins in place.

The fix: set one of the motors to Reverse so "forward" really goes forward on both sides.
2e40a9|Test carefully first: tell the robot to "drive forward" — if it spins, nine times out of ten you're missing a Reverse.
f8c0bb|Try it: is Reverse set right?
337b80|The left and right motors are mounted in opposite directions. Switch each motor's Reverse on or off and see how the robot moves when you press "forward".
622aef|🔄 spins in place (one side forward, one side backward)
f52258|Just set "one" of the motors to Reverse
e7954f|It only goes straight when "exactly one" is reversed; if both are reversed it spins too.
feb011|How many Smart Ports does the Brain have?
9c83ca|The VEX IQ Brain has 12 Smart Ports.
da29bb|The left and right motors are mounted in opposite directions and the program tells both to go forward, but the robot spins in place. What's the most likely cause?
01117c|One side going forward and the other backward makes it spin; set one of them to Reverse and it's fixed.
20fb23|The motor is actually plugged into Port 5. Which port should you pick in Devices?
d50d42|Whichever port it's really plugged into, Devices must pick the same port number.
3babaf|Deliberately get it wrong once so you know what wrong looks like.
c23ace|Plug a motor into Port 1, pick Port 1 in Devices too, and run it briefly.
77fa65|Deliberately change Devices to Port 2, run again and watch what happens.
091cf5|Change it back. Then leave both left and right motors un-reversed and watch how the robot moves.
0b8a1d|Record three tests: how you set it, how the robot moved, and your conclusion.
f5d44c|The program is written. To make the robot run on its own away from the computer, what must you do first?
7d714b|The program must first be sent to the Brain before the Brain can run it on its own.
7bddb2|The program must be downloaded to the Brain

adede9|

A program you write on the computer doesn't run on the robot automatically. You must first Download it to the Brain so the Brain has a copy. After downloading, you can unplug the computer and pick the program on the Brain to run.

You can connect with a USB cable or Bluetooth.
10ca42|How to run a program in a match

b7bdaf|

There's no computer at the match. You download the program at home first, then at the field pick the program you want on the Brain and press run. That's how an Autonomous Coding Skills run (1 minute on program alone) begins.
ae1b5c|Before the match, run the program on the Brain several times to make sure you pick the right one.
c73b31|Not enough battery, and everything acts strange

fc8a78|

When the battery is low, motors get weaker and behavior becomes unstable: the same program runs accurately today and drifts tomorrow. So always fully charge before testing and before matches.
1cf2bb|If the same program "suddenly gets better" or "suddenly gets worse", check the battery first, then suspect the program.

49f7d4|Which block does a block program start running from?
c52943|Blocks that aren't attached under "when started" won't run on their own.

4a917c|

On the left of VEXcode are the block categories (Drivetrain, Sound, Screen, Sensing, Control…); in the middle is your workspace, where you drag blocks and stack them one after another.

To use a motor or sensor, first add the device in Devices so the matching block category appears.
f3a5bf|The program's starting point: when started

509f36|

Blocks must be attached under "when started" to run. A block sitting alone off to the side just sits there and doesn't run.

Execution goes top to bottom, one block finishing before the next.
627d81|Dragging blocks out but forgetting to attach them to "when started" is the step beginners miss most.

50e0ee|

Want to try a different approach but worried about breaking things? Use Save As and the old version is kept. Then write in your engineering notebook "how this version differs from the last".

Judges like seeing this too: you tried, you compared, you recorded.
bfd799|You could name files like: straight_v1, straight_v2_tuned_speed.

cb52ed|Four-sided frame: pushed out of shape
e43749|Push on a four-sided frame and on a triangular frame. Which skews more easily?
2f8711|A four-sided frame can be pushed into a parallelogram; a triangle can't.

17e150|

The lengths of a triangle's three sides decide its shape, so it doesn't skew. A four-sided frame has fixed side lengths but can still change shape (into a parallelogram), so it is easily pushed out of shape.
f3fd06|You'll see lots of triangles in bridges, towers, and bicycle frames.
887660|Add a brace = turn a four-sided frame into two triangles

12e2ce|

Is the robot's chassis or arm wobbly? First find where the "four-sided frame" is and add a diagonal brace — it becomes two triangles and is instantly stable.

bf75aa|
  • Using only one pin at a joint makes it wobble; fixing at two or more points is steadier.
  • Put heavy parts (battery, Brain) low and near the middle so the robot is less likely to tip when turning, accelerating or bumping.
6b813f|A battery on top and off to one side is the easiest way to tip over when turning.
a0d984|Push hard on a four-sided frame, then add a brace and compare how much it skews.
5bb6b6|With the same force, it skews very little when braced.
948e7a|The robot's arm keeps wobbling. What should you do first?
b61a93|Find the four-sided spots and add diagonal braces
d0f4e1|A brace turns a four-sided frame into two triangles, making the structure instantly stable.
86276c|Where should a heavy battery go so the robot tips less easily?
a40367|The lower and more central the center of gravity, the steadier.
b3f8a6|Two beams are joined with only one pin. What happens?
d0621e|One pin is just a pivot; you need two points to hold it fixed.
d2715a|Build a four-sided frame from 4 beams and 4 pins and push it by hand to see if it skews.
b2b8d6|Add one brace, push with the same force and compare.

ecdeda|When a wheel makes one full turn, about how far does the robot move?
c27f33|If the wheel doesn't slip, one turn covers a length of ground equal to the "circumference".

5c4e80|

Picture rolling a wheel along the ground. In one turn it "measures" a stretch of ground exactly as long as the distance around the wheel — that length is the circumference.

Circumference = diameter × 3.14 (use 3.14 for π)
813352|The diameter is "the whole line through the center"; the radius is only half of it.

d1e763|

Distance = turns × circumference
Turns = distance ÷ circumference

Example: wheel diameter 60 mm, circumference about 188 mm. To go 940 mm: 940 ÷ 188 = 5 turns.
f53275|Multiplying the radius by 3.14 gives only half the circumference! Convert to diameter first.
99bfce|"drive forward for □ mm" in the program

dd7445|

When you write 200 mm in a block, VEXcode uses the wheel size you set to convert it into how many turns the motor must make. So if the wheel size is set wrong, the distance will be off.
8751b5|Change the wheel size and number of turns and see how far the robot goes.
242770|Double the diameter, same turns, and the distance doubles too.
c7e8f3|Wheel diameter 50 mm, 4 turns. About how far does it go? (use π = 3.14)
a495c4|To go 628 mm with a wheel circumference of 157 mm, how many turns?
fca54c|You switch to a bigger wheel and still turn it 3 times. What happens?
faf4e7|A bigger diameter means a bigger circumference, so one turn goes farther.
fd7981|Measure the wheel and check the distance
be9af2|Measure the wheel's diameter (mm) with a ruler and work out the circumference.
70252b|Compare with your calculation, note the error and think about why it happened.
da6f86|Write down: diameter, calculated distance, actual distance, the error and possible reasons.

507671|

In reality wheels slip a little and floor friction varies, so the measured distance is usually a bit less than calculated. The most reliable approach in competition: calculate first, then measure for real, and fine-tune using the measurement.
590aee|A small gear drives a big gear. What does the big gear do?
3a3e29|Two meshing gears turn in opposite directions

766999|

When two gears mesh, if one turns clockwise the other turns counterclockwise. To make two wheels turn the same way, add one more gear in between.

bf5f65|

A 12-tooth small gear driving a 36-tooth big gear: the small gear must turn 3 times for the big gear to turn once. 3× slower, about 3× more force. Good for an arm lifting heavy things.

The other way around, big drives small, is a speed-up: faster, but less force.
4442b9|Speed and force are like a seesaw: to get more force you give up speed.

4c2fb8|

Driven turns = driving turns × driving teeth ÷ driven teeth

Example: driving 12 teeth turns 6 times, driven 36 teeth: 6 × 12 ÷ 36 = 2 turns.
9aca17|Don't swap the tooth counts! If "driving ÷ driven" is less than 1, it's slower.
aa8b3f|Change the two gears' tooth counts and see the driven gear's turns, speed and force.
d54edd|Small drives big: fewer turns, more force; big drives small: the opposite.
150e7a|A 12-tooth driving gear turns 9 times and drives a 36-tooth gear. How many times does the driven gear turn?
97bdb1|An arm needs to lift something heavy. Which should you use?
d36697|Reduction gives big force — good for lifting.
8dc65f|Two gears mesh. The driving gear turns clockwise. The driven gear turns?
a6ac53|Two meshing gears turn in opposite directions.
3524f4|Turn the 12-tooth gear by hand 3 times and count how many times the 36-tooth turns (it should be 1).
3b09da|Swap to a 36-tooth driving a 12-tooth and measure again.
e1931a|Record both setups: driving turns, driven turns, and whether they match your formula.
653c0c|The left wheel goes forward and the right wheel backward (same speed). What does the robot do?
2e52c9|Opposite directions on the two sides make it turn in place.
27ef16|Differential drive: turning by left/right wheel speed

515d7f|

For a robot with drive wheels on the left and right, turning isn't done with a steering wheel but by making the left and right wheel speeds different:

  • Same direction, same speed → straight
  • Opposite directions → turn in place
  • One side faster, one slower → arcs toward the slower side
cca345|Want a straight line but it drifts?

665439|

If the two sides have different speed or friction, it drifts. This is the most common cause of "won't go straight". Fix: check whether a wheel is stuck, whether both sides have the same Reverse and speed settings, and if needed correct it with the Gyro.
daed94|Measure first: drive straight 1000 mm — how far did it drift and to which side? Then guess why.
db1df5|How much to turn, how much the wheels turn

b48f69|

Turning 180° needs twice as much wheel rotation as turning 90°. Omni wheels have low resistance when turning in place and can also slide sideways.
d7a54f|"Turn 90 degrees" is the angle the robot's body turns, not the angle the wheels turn.
566cb3|Change the left and right wheel speeds and see how the robot moves.
4e864a|Both wheels equally fast → straight; one positive, one negative → turn in place.
c59ec8|Left wheel 70%, right wheel 30%. Which way does the robot arc?
76a563|The left wheel is faster and the right is slower, so it arcs toward the slower side (right).
dff7bf|To turn in place, the left and right wheels should be?
082122|Only opposite directions turn it in place.
dfd3d9|The wheel rotation needed to turn 180° is how many times that for 90°?
bfec46|Double the angle, double the rotation.
a86d38|Make the robot "drive forward for 1000 mm".
780559|Measure how far it drifted and to which side.
465913|Guess the cause, change just one thing (like checking the wheels or resetting) and test again.
181baf|Write down what you changed and how the drift changed — three tests is enough.
09e3a4|The longer the arm, lifting the same weight is?
99bc85|The farther the load from the pivot (the longer the lever arm), the harder the motor works.
1c5e60|Lever arm: farther from the pivot is harder

60b0b7|

The arm's pivot is like a seesaw's fulcrum. The farther the load is from the fulcrum (the longer the lever arm), the more force is needed. To lift heavy things: keep the arm short.

413056|

A motor driving an arm directly often can't lift. Add a small-drives-big reduction gear set (like 12:36): force goes up, the arm slows down, and it lifts steadily.
197699|Also set the stopping mode to "hold" so the arm doesn't slowly sink after lifting.

473bd0|

Gripping relies on friction. Smooth plastic slips easily, so use rubber or rubber bands on the claw's contact surfaces for a firmer grip.

f03aa6|

Find a need → think of ideas → build a prototype → test → improve. Don't aim for perfect at once — build it first; testing shows what to change.
